lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task: plan: the fair-distribution plan

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to plan before computing anything.

items.prompt: 29 students need vans that hold 8 students each. How many vans are needed?

steps: The 5 leftover students still need a van.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: 83 students are going on a field trip. Each van holds 4 students. How many vans are needed so every student has a seat?
A baker has 66 eggs and needs 5 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will figure out, how, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A baker has 202 eggs and needs 9 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: 219 students are going on a field trip. Each van holds 6 students. How many vans are needed so every student has a seat?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
